title: Manage services
description: Start, stop, restart, or enable system services on remote hosts using an ad-hoc command with the service module.

breakdown.meaning: Target the 'webservers' host group
Use the service module to manage systemd/init services
Restart the nginx service
Become root (sudo) — required for service management

flags.description: Name of the service to manage
Desired state: started, stopped, restarted, reloaded
Whether the service starts on boot (yes/no)
Reload systemd manager configuration before acting (yes/no)

example: ansible webservers -m service -a "name=nginx state=restarted enabled=yes" -b -i inventory.yml
tip: Use 'state=reloaded' instead of 'state=restarted' when possible to avoid dropping active connections. In playbooks, use handlers to restart services only when config changes.

title: Gather facts

breakdown.meaning: Target all hosts in the inventory

Timeout in seconds for fact gathering

tip: Use 'gather_subset=min' in playbooks to speed up execution when you only need basic facts. Filter with wildcards like 'ansible_mem*' to quickly find memory-related facts.

title: Template module in playbook
description: Use the template module in a playbook to render Jinja2 templates with host-specific variables and deploy them as configuration files on remote hosts.

breakdown.meaning: Ansible module that processes Jinja2 templates
Local Jinja2 template file
Remote destination path for the rendered file
Jinja2 syntax to insert variable values into the template

flags.description: Path to the local Jinja2 template file (.j2)
Remote path where the rendered file is written
Owner of the destination file
Group of the destination file
File permissions (e.g., '0644')
Create backup before overwriting (yes/no)
Command to validate the file before putting it in place (e.g., 'nginx -t -c %s')

example:
# Playbook task:
- name: Deploy nginx config from template
  template:
    src: templates/nginx.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
    backup: yes
    validate: 'nginx -t -c %s'
  notify: restart nginx

# templates/nginx.conf.j2:
server {
    listen {{ http_port }};
    server_name {{ server_name }};
    root {{ document_root }};
}
output:
TASK [Deploy nginx config from template] ************************

    "checksum": "d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3",

    "owner": "root",

tip: Use the validate parameter to test configs before deploying (e.g., 'nginx -t -c %s' or 'visudo -cf %s'). This prevents deploying broken configs that could crash services.

tip: Run --check --diff in CI on every pull request to generate a change preview before any deployment. Not all modules support check mode — a task that fails in check mode does not guarantee failure in real mode either.

title: Encrypt inline string
description: Encrypt a single string value for embedding directly in a playbook or vars file, without encrypting the whole file.

breakdown.meaning: Ansible encryption tool
Encrypt a single string (not a whole file)
The plaintext string to encrypt
Variable name to wrap around the encrypted output in YAML

flags.description: Encrypt a single string for inline use in YAML
Variable name to wrap the encrypted value in
Use a labelled vault ID for multiple vault passwords
Read the string from stdin rather than the command line

tip: Prefer encrypt_string over full-file encryption for individual credentials — the rest of your vars file stays readable in git. Always pass the value via stdin (--stdin-name) rather than as a command argument to avoid it appearing in shell history.

title: Capture task output
description: Store a task's return value in a variable using register, then use it in subsequent tasks for conditionals, debug output, or further processing.

breakdown.meaning: Capture the full return value of the task into a variable named result
Standard output from the command as a string
Return code of the command (0 = success)
stdout split into a list of lines for easy iteration
Conditional that runs this task only if the previous command succeeded

example:
- name: Check disk usage
  command: df -h /
  register: disk_result

- name: Show disk output
  debug:
    msg: "{{ disk_result.stdout }}"
  when: disk_result.rc == 0
tip: Register captures the full module return dict — use result.stdout for command output, result.stat for stat module, result.json for uri module. Always check result.failed before acting on output to handle partial failures gracefully.

title: Loop over a list
description: Repeat a task for each item in a list using the loop directive — the modern replacement for the older with_items syntax.

breakdown.meaning: Iterate over each item in the list — modern replacement for with_items
First item in the loop list
Second item in the loop list
Jinja2 placeholder for the current loop value
Optional block to customise loop variable name or label output

example:
- name: Install required packages
  apt:
    name: "{{ item }}"
    state: present
  loop:
    - nginx
    - postgresql
    - redis-server
  become: true
output:
TASK [Install required packages] ********************************
ok: [web-1] => (item=nginx)
changed: [web-1] => (item=postgresql)
changed: [web-1] => (item=redis-server)
tip: Define the list in group_vars or defaults rather than inline to keep tasks clean: loop: "{{ required_packages }}". For complex objects, loop over a list of dicts and reference fields with item.name, item.version etc.

title: Conditional task execution
description: Use the when directive to run or skip tasks based on facts, registered variables, or inventory variables — conditions are Jinja2 expressions evaluated per host.

breakdown.meaning: Only run this task if the Jinja2 expression evaluates to true
True on Ubuntu and Debian hosts (from gathered facts)
True on RHEL, CentOS, and Rocky Linux hosts
Condition based on a previously registered task result
Skip this task when running in --check dry-run mode

example:
- name: Install nginx (Debian)
  apt:
    name: nginx
    state: present
  when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"

- name: Install nginx (RedHat)
  yum:
    name: nginx
    state: present
  when: ansible_os_family == "RedHat"
output:
TASK [Install nginx (Debian)] ************************************
ok: [ubuntu-web-1]
skipping: [centos-web-1]

TASK [Install nginx (RedHat)] ************************************
skipping: [ubuntu-web-1]
changed: [centos-web-1]
tip: When conditions as a list act as implicit AND — each line must be true. Use 'or' and 'and' for compound expressions: when: ansible_memtotal_mb > 2048 and ansible_os_family == "Debian". Undefined variables are falsy, so guard with is defined: when: my_var is defined.

title: Notify handlers
description: Handlers are tasks triggered by notify at the end of a play — they run once regardless of how many tasks notify them, making them ideal for service restarts triggered by config changes.

breakdown.meaning: Queue the named handler to run at end of play, but only if this task reported changed
Play section defining handler task definitions
Handler name — must exactly match the string used in notify
Any Ansible module can be used in a handler task
Force all queued handlers to run immediately at this point in the play

example:
- name: Deploy nginx config
  template:
    src: nginx.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  notify: restart nginx

handlers:
  - name: restart nginx
    service:
      name: nginx
      state: restarted
output:
TASK [Deploy nginx config] ***************************************
changed: [web-1]

RUNNING HANDLER [restart nginx] *********************************
changed: [web-1]

PLAY RECAP *******************************************************
web-1 : ok=2  changed=2  unreachable=0  failed=0
tip: Handlers run once per play regardless of how many tasks notify them — three tasks notifying restart nginx produces one restart. Use meta: flush_handlers when a subsequent task depends on the service already being restarted before the play ends.
